en: One fascicle of the Secret Recitation Ritual of Vajrarāja Bodhisattva.
Compiled by Kai-fu-yi-tong-san-si Te-jin Shi Hong-lu-qing, Duke of Su State.

The Imperial Preceptor, holding a fief of three thousand households, invested with the purple robe and posthumously honored as Minister of Works, bearing the posthumous title Dajian (Great Mirror), and styled Dayangzhi (Great Extensive Wisdom), the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple, translated by imperial decree: "I now take pity upon all who seek equal enlightenment."
Alternatively, not knowing this secret yoga that swiftly accomplishes the Buddha-dharma,
one endures various ascetic practices for three great asaṃkhyeya kalpas,
yet fails to reach unsurpassed bodhi.
Out of compassion for them,
I have here briefly set forth from among the hundred thousand verses of the *Vajraśekhara*,

the ritual procedure for the recitation of the Bodhisattva Vajrarāja— the alternate name for the Enjoyment Body manifested for others that flows forth from the Great Perfect Mirror-like Wisdom of the Svābhāvika-siddhi Dharmakāya of the Tathāgata Vairocana.
By practicing the great mudrās and other rites through the three secrets,
the bodhisattvas who practice mantra can swiftly realize the state of the Tathāgata’s perfect enlightenment.
They attain the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*),
abide on the great stage of Samantabhadra,
and [remain] within the inexhaustible realm of birth and death (*saṃsāra*).
He tames all sentient beings,
causing them all to dwell securely in unsurpassed bodhi,
without ever experiencing weariness.
First, one should carefully examine and gain thorough understanding of a Vajraśekhara-yoga ācārya,
and seek to receive the empowerments of the five families or the vidyādhara empowerment.
If one does not understand how to discern [the truth], one will fall into ruin oneself.
Having encountered a genuine ācārya, one should conceive of him as the appearance of a Tathāgata and offer all excellent and sublime worldly requisites to him.
Why is this? Because this vehicle of the supreme dharma is that which all Buddhas of the three periods of time have collectively followed and upheld;
therefore, one should inquire about each and every point within this dharma.

He caused them all to fully comprehend the mandala rites, the image-painting rites, the self-consecration rites, the five types of secret methods beginning with the pacification rite (*śāntika*), the four seals (*mudrā*), the great seal (*mahāmudrā*), the single seal (*ekamudrā*),
the accomplishment of the body through the five wisdoms (*pañcajñāna*), the empowerment of the three secrets (*triguhyādhiṣṭhāna*), and the secret offerings.
All must be thoroughly mastered.
If a bodhisattva of mantra practice is to abide in the great bodhicitta, [they must do so].
Because one dedicates the merit performed toward the fruit of equal enlightenment,
one quickly attains Buddhahood through the benefit of great compassion.
Were it otherwise, [one would not].
Not only will one fail to attain siddhi,
but this is called slandering all Buddhas;
one will certainly fall into the three evil realms.
If whatever one intends to do or has done is for the sake of awakening and the benefit of sentient beings,
then whatever one seeks and aspires for will be accomplished without exception.
Once the practitioner of mantras has received the dharma, [this shall come to pass].
One should establish a maṇḍala, install the honored image, and don new, clean garments.
Following the yoga method, one should perform recitation during the four periods of the day;
at least two periods must never be omitted.
One should always remain in accord with the samādhi of constant joy.
When first entering the maṇḍala to prostrate to the Buddha,
one kneels long and joins both hands like an opening lotus flower.
This is called the Mantra and Mudrā for Purifying the Vessel-like Realm.
The mantra is: Oṃ rājopagata sarvadharma [svāhā]. Recite this while forming the aforementioned mudrā to purify the three karmas.
The mantra for empowering the four places is as follows:
*oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’haṃ*. Then, one should form the Vajrotthāpana mudrā.
With both hands in vajra-fists,
the thumbs and ring fingers hook each other,
while the heads of the index and middle fingers touch one another on their sides.
When wishing to form this mudrā,
first visualize five wisdom-vajras at the hearts and tongues of both hands.
Seal it three times.
Recite this mantra to awaken all Tathāgatas throughout the entirety of space, saying:
Oṃ vairo tistha. Having recited it once for each seal, raise [the hands] once.
One should then visualize all Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, filling the realm of empty space. Thereafter,
one extends both arms upward above the crown of the head,
performs the vajra-pañjali mudrā, and fully stretches out the two feet.
Prostrating oneself upon the ground,
one pays homage to the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the East.
The mantra for offering one's body is as follows:
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-pūjopasthānāyātmanā niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajrasattva-adhiṣṭhasva māṃ hūṃ. One should recite thus.
Desiring to serve and make offerings to all Tathāgatas,
I now offer my own body;
may all Tathāgatas look upon me with compassion.
Then, drawing the two feet together,
place the vajra-pañjali at the heart and touch the forehead to the ground.
Pay homage to the Tathāgata Ratnasambhava of the South.
The mantra for offering one’s body is:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāpraśādhanam niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajraratnapraśāda svāhā. Contemplate thus.
Desiring to make offerings to all Tathāgatas and to request empowerment,
I now offer my own body.
May all Tathāgatas confer upon me the empowerment with the vajra-jewel.
Furthermore, placing the palms together upon the crown of the head and touching the mouth to the ground,
one pays homage to the Tathāgata Amitāyus of the western quarter.
The mantra for offering one’s body is:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāpravartanāya tmanam niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajradharmapravartaya māṃ kṛta. One should contemplate in this manner.
Now, for the sake of making successive offerings to all Tathāgatas, I offer my own body.
May all Tathāgatas turn the Vajra Dharma-wheel for me. Then, place the vajra-palms upon the heart.
Placing the crown of one's head upon the ground, one pays homage to the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi of the north and recites the mantra of offering:

*Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjākarmānugrahāya me sarvatathāgatavajrakarma kuru maḥ*. One should form this thought: *Oṃ, for the sake of my service to all the Tathāgatas, grant me the vajra-activity of all the Tathāgatas.*
Now, for the sake of performing the activities of making offerings to all Tathāgatas, I offer my own body.
May all Tathāgatas perform the vajra-activities for me. Then, he places his right knee upon the ground.
Form the Vajradhara mudrā and place it upon the crown of the head;
imagine that one is universally prostrating at the feet of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
With the left hand covering and the right hand facing upward, hook the thumbs and little fingers together.
This is the mudrā; the mantra is as follows:
Next, perform the rejoicing, the invitation, the dedication, and the aspiration;
then sit in the half-lotus posture with both hands in vajra-fists placed upon the two knees,
[focusing] on the heart, the tongue, and the two hands.
The syllable HŪṂ radiates golden light, like the Bhagavān abiding in the posture of preaching the Dharma;
his body rests upon a pure moon disc as if seated upon a polished mirror,
its brilliance pervading the entire realm of phenomena.
Purifying the realm of sentient beings everywhere, one gazes upon the Buddha in the sky with the Mātaṅga eye;
turning the gaze to survey the eight directions,
one scatters vajra flames, performing the binding of the boundary and the expulsion of obstructors.
Next, while abiding in the samādhi of the four immeasurable minds within the adamantine city of the [respective] locations,
one visualizes the Karma-vajra within the moon disc of the heart;
with great compassion, one cuts through the suffering of all sentient beings.
The mantra for visualizing the Karma-cakra pervading the entire Dharma-realm is:
Oṃ mahākāruṇya sapāra. Next, one should exercise a mind of compassion, employing the Karma-cakra throughout the realm of sentient beings.
The mantra for bestowing immeasurable bliss is:
Oṃ mahā-maitrīya-sphara. Next, with a joyful mind, one should employ the karma-cakra.
The mantra for pervading the realm of sentient beings is:

Oṃ sarvaśuddhapramocana-spharaṇa-citta-karmacakre sarvasattvadhātum sphara. This is the wheel of the activity of the mind that radiates the liberation of all-purity throughout the realm of sentient beings.
The mantra for accomplishing great equanimity is:
Oṃ mahā-vikṣipta-sphara. Next, bind the Vajra-joined-palms mudrā by interlacing the ten fingers of both hands, with the right pressing over the left; then recite the Vajra-joined-palms mantra:
Oṃ vairocani. Using this same previous mudrā, one then forms the Vajrasphoṭa mudrā and recites the Vajrasphoṭa mantra:
Oṃ vajrasphoṭa. Next, one binds the Heart-opening Mudrā.
First, visualize the syllable TRA on the right breast and the syllable THA on the left breast;
imagine these two syllables as the leaves of a door.
First, perform the binding mudrā by striking it against the heart.
The mantra for opening it with three tugs is:
Oṃ vajra-bandha traṭ (the *traṭ* is pronounced as a single syllable). Next, one cubit in front [of oneself], visualize an eight-petaled lotus.
Upon that flower, place the syllable *Aḥ*.
It emits great light, white like crystal.
Then, with the vajra-bond mudrā, bring forth the two winds.
As if grasping that syllable and placing it within the palace of the heart, the mantra is:
Oṃ vajravedha ḥ. Having thus placed the syllable, it becomes vividly manifest within the heart.
Next, perform the Vajra-bond:
join the two thumbs, bending them together into the palms;
then, with the two index fingers, each bent, support the backs of the two thumbs.
Touching the chest with the mudrā, the mantra is:
Oṃ vajramuṣṭi maṃ. Having thus closed the door of the heart, one should visualize that syllable as clearly established.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of Samantabhadra.
Extending and joining the two fire-fingers (the middle fingers) in the vajra-bind, recite the mantra once:
Oṃ samayas tvaṃ. Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of Joyful Delight.
As in the previous binding,
join the palms with the thumbs and ring fingers interlocked;
the thumbs and little fingers are both extended upward and joined.
With this arrow of great desire, one shoots at those of the three vehicles. The mantra is:
Oṃ samaya hūḥ sara ta satvaṃ. Next, bind the seal of the supreme three times.
With both hands in vajra-fists, hook the backs of the thumbs and wisdom fingers together;
straighten the two index fingers (vāyu) respectively. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sunva sunva hūṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ ānaya hoḥ bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ. With this mudrā, turning it counter-clockwise, perform the ritual of warding off obstacles.
Rotate the hands clockwise to form the boundary seal (*sīmābandha*).
Next, form the concentration seal (*samādhi-mudrā*):
interlace the two palms with the backs facing outward and place them palms-up, level with the lower abdomen.
To perform the mantra of the *samādhi-padmahṛdaya* with the power of exertion, one should recite:
Oṃ samādhi-padma-hṛd. Then, sitting upright with the body straight, one should reflect as follows:
All phenomena arise from one's own mind;
from the very beginning, they have never existed.
Having entered the samādhi of cessation, [one realizes this].
He then further beheld in the void of space countless Buddhas,
as numerous as sesame seeds filling the entire earth, beyond all calculation.
At that time, those Buddhas each extended their right hands.
Snapping his fingers to awaken him, he said to the practitioner:
"Good son, that which you have realized is but a single path of purity;
you have not yet realized the ocean of omniscience."
One should recollect the bodhicitta and accomplish all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra.
Having heard this exhortation, the practitioner—
Observing one's own body,
one should prostrate before each of the Buddhas and address them, saying:
"What is called the bodhicitta?
The Buddhas replied, "Observe the letter-gateway within the heart;
its original nature is pure, like the full moon."
The mantra for bestowal is:
Oṃ citrapratiṣṭhe ḍiṅkaromi. The practitioner, following these instructions, silently recites it once and then visualizes their own mind as a pure, full moon.
At that time, the Buddhas spoke again as follows:
"Son of good family, such is the essential nature and characteristic of the bodhicitta.
They then bestowed the mantra, saying:
Oṃ ṛddhivati svāhā. Having silently recited this once, the practitioner reflects thus:
"The essence of the bodhicitta is firm and stable."
Then, upon the lunar disc, one should visualize the five-pronged vajra of the five wisdoms. The mantra is:
Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra. Visualize the vajra as being like the color of gold.
Pure light is emitted within the lunar disc,
as transparent inside and out as crystal.
Furthermore, contemplate this Vajra mantra, vast and pervasive throughout the Dharma-realm, which says:
Oṃ sarvavajra-āveśa vajra. Then, gradually withdrawing, all the Tathāgatas present in the empty space of that location merge into a single essence.
The mantra for stopping [the visualization] at a size equal to one's own body is:
Oṃ saṃhara vajra. Furthermore, one should perform this contemplation:
"May this body of mine now become a vajra-body. The mantra is: [Oṃ vajrībhava].
Oṃ vajra-tma-kuhaṃ. Knowing oneself to be the five wisdom-vajras,
one then transforms into the body of the principal deity,
which has four arms.
The upper two hands form the gesture of an upright arrow;
the lower right hand is turned upward at the heart holding a vajra;
the lower left hand forms a vajra-fist.
He holds a vajra-bell at his left waist;
his brow is knit, yet his mouth smiles, and he is white in color.
He wears a crown of the five Buddhas, a vermilion skirt, and celestial garments.
Sitting in the half-lotus posture upon a lotus flower within a moon disc, one should immediately form the root mudrā:
with both hands in vajra-fists, hook the thumbs (tarjanī), middle fingers (madhyamā), and ring fingers (anāmikā) together. This is that mudrā; recite the mantra as follows:
Having empowered the four places— the heart, forehead, throat, and crown— with the *ṭakki hūṃ jaḥ* mudrā,
one should then form the Vajradhātu-īśvara mudrā by firmly binding [the hands] and extending the two fire fingers (*teja-aṅguli*).
Bend the first fingers so they touch each other and extend the two [index fingers] against the back; the mantra is:
Oṃ bu khaṃ. One should place the seal upon the crown of the head and recite the aforementioned mantra.
Next, the mantra for placing [the seal] on the forehead is:
Oṃ vajrasattva. Next, the mantra for placing [the seal] on the right side of the crown is:
Oṃ vajraratna. Next, the mantra for placing [the seal] behind the crown is:
Oṃ vajradharma. Next, for the mantra of the crown of the head, it is said:
Oṃ vajrakarma. Then, place the vajra-fist upon the forehead.
After directing [the breath] toward the crown of the head,
extend the two winds and perform three circumambulations; then,
let them unfold sequentially from the earth element (*pṛthivī*).
From the two shoulders downward, form the gesture of a garland sash.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajramāle viśvamukhe. Next, visualize the two syllables Oṃ and Chiṃ upon the two wind-wheels.
Oṃ. From the right [hand], a green light emerges like a lotus fiber;
it then forms a green cord that circles three times around the heart.
Next, [touch] the back of the navel and the two knees.
Then move back to the navel, next to the lower back, then to the heart.
Next, [touch] the right and left shoulders.
Next, [the hands] move to the neck, then the forehead, then the crown of the head;
thereafter, they perform the gesture of draping celestial robes as before,
while reciting the two syllables OṂ CAṂ.
Next, perform the mudrā of Delightful Joy (Ratimodana), the Vajrabandha, and recite the mantra of the three strikes:
Oṃ vajra tuṣya hūḥ. Then, visualize within a pure moon disc the syllable HŪṂ.
Transforming into the Honored One,
one then forms the Vajra-Entry Mudrā. Having bound it,
with both thumbs joined together and inserted into the palms, the mantra is recited as follows:
Oṃ vajrasattva a. Again, recite this mantra: Oṃ vajrasattva niriṣya.
Next, summon [the deities] into one's own body using the four mudrās and the four vidyās.
First, with joy, one should recite the mantra for the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) using the two *ra* syllables:
*Oṃ vajrasatva hūṃ phaṭ*. As for that which was previously visualized, it constitutes the Dharma Body (*dharmakāya*).
That which is now being contemplated constitutes the wisdom-body (*jñānakāya*),
for the [visualized] forms and [the mind] are conjoined to manifest as a single entity.
Next, one should adorn the world with this mind by means of the gate of offering.
Within the maṇḍala, visualize a white lotus with a wondrous-colored vajra stem;
it has eight petals, complete with filaments and anthers, naturally adorned with various jewels,
constantly emitting immeasurable light, and surrounded by hundreds of thousands of other lotuses.
Upon that, one further visualizes the Great Awakened One’s lion throne adorned with the king of jewels; within the great palace,
jeweled pillars stand in rows, and everywhere there are various banners and canopies.
Intertwined with pearl garlands and the like, draped with exquisite robes of precious jewels,
surrounded by clouds of incense and flowers, and clouds of various gems,
they rain down a profusion of diverse blossoms that scatter in profusion to adorn the ground.
Harmonizing with the wondrous celestial sounds, they perform various musical offerings;
within the palace, one visualizes pure and sublime things:
auspicious vases, argha-offerings, and the blossoming king of jewel-trees, illuminated by mani-lamps.
Samādhi and dhāraṇī are their grounds; the perfections of the Buddha are their sovereign ladies-in-waiting.
Skillful means compose the various female musicians, singing the wondrous sounds of the sublime Dharma as exquisite flowers that adorn enlightenment.
By the power of my merit, the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment,
and the power of the Dharma-realm, I abide in universal offering.
Then, recite the mantra of the Great Treasury of Space:
Oṃ gagaṇasvabhāva vajra hūṃ. Recite this three times, and all the virtuous aspirations arising therefrom shall be accomplished.
Next, within the moon disc upon the lion throne in the center of the maṇḍala.
Visualize the syllable Oṃ as becoming the principal deity.
In front of the principal deity,
place the syllable Ma as the Mind-born Vajra.
To the right, place *ha* as Kīlikīla-vajra;
behind, place *su* as Rāga-vajra;
to the left, place *kha* as Māna-vajra.
In the northwest corner, one should place *vaḥ* as the Vajrī Citta-utpannā;
in the northeast corner, one should place *vīra* as the Vajrī Kṛtī.
In the southeast corner, one installs Sā as the Vajrī Saṃtoṣā;
in the southwest corner, one installs Tva as the Vajrī Manasvinī;
and in the center of the eastern gate, one installs Rū as the Bodhisattva Rūpa.
In the southern gate, one installs the syllable HŪṂ as the Bodhisattva of Sound.
In the western gate, one installs the syllable VAṂ as the Bodhisattva of Fragrance.
In the northern gate, one installs the syllable HRĪḤ as the Bodhisattva of Taste.
In the northwest corner of the outer courtyard, install the Bodhisattva Suveśa as the Season of Spring;
in the northeast corner, install the Bodhisattva Raveśa as the Season of Rain;
and in the southeast corner, install the Bodhisattva Taveśa as the Season of Autumn.
In the southwest corner, one should install the syllables *sa* and *tvaṃ* joined together as the Bodhisattva Śiśira.
Next, one should place the syllable *oṃ* upon the heart of the painted image;
on both sides of this syllable, one should place the syllable *ya* to constitute the principal deity.
Then, perform the mudrās of the hook, noose, chain, and bell to invite [the deity].
With both hands in vajra-fists, the thumbs (earth-wheels) are turned inward to hook [the deity], while the two index fingers (wind-wheels) are held straight;
the right index finger is bent like a hook.
Having performed the binding, recite the mantra and beckon three times with the right *vāyu* (ring finger); this is the *vajrāṅkuśa* (Vajra Hook).
Then, without changing this previous mudrā, recite the mantra: join the two *vāyu* fingers face-to-face.
Interlace them so that they form a ring; this is the mantra of the Vajrapāśa.
Without altering the pāśa-mudrā, hook the two vāyu fingers together in reverse.
This is the Vajra Chain. Then, recite the mantra without altering the previous mudrā:
join both earth fingers and both wind fingers so that their tips meet; this is the Vajra Bell.
The mantra says:
By forming the vajra-hook seal, one immediately causes the principal deity to descend;
by the vajra-noose seal, one is able to summon the noble ones.
By means of the vajra-shackle mudrā, one is able to cause [the deity] to remain;
by binding the vajra-bell, one can delight all the noble ones.
Next, one should offer arghya water.
Forming the Vajra-joined palms mudrā,
tilting it flat toward the left,
press it upon the vessel while reciting the mantra, and then offer it.
The mantra is:
Oṃ paramasukhaśayā sārītanamaste prasāramita namo vibhagavan damya hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ he pratīccha kuśumam arghaṃ na thothaḥ. Next, place the left vajra-fist at the side of the waist.
With the right vajra-fist held upward at the heart, the mantra is:
*HŪṂ VAJRASATTVA SARVADURĀRĀDHYA SATTVA*. Then, one employs the Vajrarāja-mudrā.
Form the gesture of grasping a bow with the left fist and the gesture of drawing an arrow with the right.
This is the Vajra-mudrā of the Mind-born; its mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajrasattva hūṃ. Next, with two vajra-fists, cross the arms by placing the right over the left and embrace the chest;
this is the mudrā of Kīlikīla-vajra, and its mantra is as follows:

Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner.

This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. With the left *vajra-muṣṭi*, support the right elbow; extend the right fist upward like the form of a banner. This is the seal (*mudrā*) of Rāgavajrī; the mantra is as follows: Oṃ vajra-hūṃ-kāri-kīli-cīca. Having emerged from the maṇḍala through the empowerment, the armor, the seal of joy,
and so forth, one should at all times abide solely in the great bodhicitta,

One attains perfect awakening even in this very life;
